[Problem on LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/rising-temperature/)

## Problem

`Weather` records a temperature for each `recordDate` (one row per date, but some dates may be missing). Return the `id` of every day that was warmer than the previous calendar day.

## Formalisation

A self-join pairs the table with itself, so we need two independent variables ranging over the same set $W$:

$$
\{\, w.\mathrm{id} \mid w, w' \in W,\ w'.\mathrm{date} = w.\mathrm{date} - 1\ \text{day},\ w.\mathrm{temp} > w'.\mathrm{temp} \,\}.
$$

Days whose previous date is missing have no partner $w'$ and so drop out, which is what we want.

## Solution

```sql
SELECT today.id
FROM Weather today
JOIN Weather yesterday
  ON yesterday.recordDate = DATE_SUB(today.recordDate, INTERVAL 1 DAY)
WHERE today.temperature > yesterday.temperature;
```

A window-function version works too, but only if it checks the gap explicitly:

```sql
WITH w AS (
  SELECT id, recordDate, temperature,
         LAG(recordDate)  OVER (ORDER BY recordDate) AS prev_date,
         LAG(temperature) OVER (ORDER BY recordDate) AS prev_temp
  FROM Weather
)
SELECT id FROM w
WHERE DATEDIFF(recordDate, prev_date) = 1
  AND temperature > prev_temp;
```

## Pitfalls

- **`date - 1` is not date arithmetic in MySQL.** It converts `'2024-03-01'` to the number 20240301 and subtracts 1, which breaks at every month boundary. Use `DATE_SUB(d, INTERVAL 1 DAY)` or `DATEDIFF(a, b)`.
- **`LAG` gives the previous *row*, not the previous *day*.** If a date is missing, `LAG` compares with an older day instead. That is the trap in this problem.
